title: Narrowing the Collaboration Gap, Probably
abstract: arXiv:2610.19215v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed as teams of agents that hold different private information about a shared task. How should such agents concisely communicate in a way that promotes aggregation of decision-relevant information? Communicating only proposed actions can discard decision-relevant uncertainty: two agents may prefer the same action for different reasons. We study an alternative interface in which agents communicate calibrated beliefs over actions. We first analyze a simple synthetic setting that captures the structure of multi-round reasoning under partial information. In this setting, we show theoretically and empirically that communicating unbiased probabilities can be strictly more powerful than communicating actions. We then test the same principle in a collaborative maze-solving task with trained transformers and pretrained LLM agents. Our results demonstrate that probability communication outperforms action

translated_title: 很可能缩小协作差距（Narrowing the Collaboration Gap, Probably）
translated_abstract: 大语言模型越来越多地被部署为由多个智能体组成的团队，这些智能体对同一个共享任务持有不同的私有信息。这样的智能体应如何以简洁的方式进行沟通，才能促进决策相关信息的汇聚？仅交流所提议的动作可能会丢弃与决策相关的不确定性：两个智能体可能出于不同的原因偏好同一个动作。我们研究了一种替代性的交互接口，即智能体之间交流关于动作的经校准的概率信念。我们首先分析了一个简单的合成场景，该场景刻画了部分信息条件下多轮推理的结构。在该场景中，我们从理论和实证上证明，传递无偏的概率可以严格优于传递动作。随后，我们在一个由经过训练的Transformer和预训练LLM智能体参与的协作迷宫求解任务中测试了同样的原则。我们的结果表明，概率沟通优于动作沟通。
tldr: 该论文提出让持有不同私有信息的多智能体通过交流关于动作的校准概率信念而非仅交流动作本身，并从理论和实验上证明这种概率沟通方式能更有效地汇聚决策相关信息、提升协作表现。
en_tdlr: This paper shows theoretically and empirically that LLM agents communicating calibrated probability beliefs over actions, rather than just proposed actions, is strictly more powerful for aggregating decision-relevant information in collaborative multi-agent tasks.
